name: Katavrin
manufacturer: Street chemist (widely produced; original formula attributed to a Shelf lab called 'Calm Hand')
description: Katavrin is an unlicensed but widely available withdrawal symptom suppressor targeting the physical horror of acute withdrawal: vomiting, muscle cramps, sweating, tremor, and autonomic instability. It doesn't address dependency or craving — it just makes the body tolerable during the worst days. Derived partly from alpha-2 adrenergic agonist chemistry with added muscle relaxant and antiemetic compounds, Katavrin is crude but effective.
side_effects: Significant hypotension — dangerous if combined with anything cardiovascular
Rebound autonomic instability on discontinuation if used more than 7 days
Variable potency between batches — Shelf production quality is inconsistent
street_price: Φ8-15 per dose depending on batch quality
cultural_context: Katavrin is the drug that makes withdrawal survivable for people who can't access clinics. On the Shelf, it's as common as painkillers — every block has someone who knows where to get it. Some Shelf medics quietly stock it and consider it essential harm-reduction material. Novafold has lobbied to have it classified as a controlled substance, allegedly because it competes with their legal alternatives, though the official justification is safety concerns about inconsistent production.
story_hooks: The Calm Hand lab that originated Katavrin has been raided — someone wants the formula suppressed, and the Shelf community that depends on it needs help rebuilding supply
A batch of Katavrin has been deliberately contaminated — someone is using the withdrawal-aid supply chain as a vector for something else
A Novafold lobbyist approaches the players about shutting down Katavrin production; the money is good, but the consequences are obvious
